issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template Stock implementation provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the specification or tests that call emptyStock() will not find it in the template and may be confused or blocked from implementing the intended behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the specification: rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a new emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory(). Ensure the method signature is public void emptyStock() to match the problem statement and solution.

issues.description: The Stock emptying method is named inconsistently: the problem statement's UML and the solution implementation use emptyStock(), but the template repository's Stock class provides clearInventory() instead. This mismatch can confuse students who are told to use/implement emptyStock() (per the exercise) but find a differently named method in the starter code, increasing extraneous cognitive load and causing mapping errors between requirements and code.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template's Stock.clearInventory() to emptyStock() to match the problem statement and solution, or add an emptyStock() wrapper that delegates to clearInventory() so starter code, requirements, and solution use the same identifier.
